# Book brief
- Non-fiction, narrative history for general readers.
- Premise: how one doctor's map of a London cholera outbreak changed public health.
- Voice: plain, vivid, present the people as real characters. Short paragraphs.
- Chapter length: 1500 to 2000 words.

# 01 The pump on Broad Street
## Questions
- When and where did the outbreak start?
- How many people died?
- What did John Snow do?
## Learnings
- [S1] The outbreak began on 31 August 1854 in Soho, London (Snow 1855, part 3).
- [S1] Snow marked each death on a street map and found that most were close to the Broad Street pump (Snow 1855, map 1).
- [S2] The outbreak killed 616 people (section Outbreak).
- [S2] The parish board removed the pump handle on 8 September 1854 at Snow's request (section Snow's work).
- [S3] The curate Henry Whitehead first doubted Snow, then traced the first case to a baby at 40 Broad Street (page Whitehead).
- [S3] A cesspool near the pump leaked into the well (page Whitehead).
